stem:
Tara mixes a small spoonful of curd into a bowl of lukewarm milk and into a bowl of cold milk. She leaves both for a few hours. Only the lukewarm milk sets into curd. The cold milk may taste a little sour but does not set the same way.

Which statement best explains this difference?

options.text: Microorganisms in the curd starter grow and multiply faster in lukewarm milk, turning it into curd.
Lukewarm milk turns into curd immediately when the starter is mixed in.
Only the cold milk forms curd; lukewarm milk stays liquid because warmth stops the starter.
Both bowls have formed curd because both can taste a little sour.

teacher.key_rationale: The starter microbes grow faster in lukewarm milk and form curd after time. Curd is not immediate; cold is not the better condition; slight sourness alone is not full curd formation.

mx_swap.reason: Boiling-hot milk CWO invents boiling not in the stem; kept condition_omission, relationship_reversal, and surface_feature_capture.
